brand_alignment.reason: Tagline 'find your magic' matches the pre-approved tagline 'Find Your Magic' on the BRAND-GL-2026-001 approved list (case-insensitive match — confirm casing is title-case in final creative). No banned words from the BRAND-GL-2026-001 list ('cheap', 'basic', 'last chance', 'clearance blowout', 'dirt cheap', 'unbeatable', 'lowest prices anywhere', 'nobody beats Macys') appear in the campaign copy. However, the copy uses 'free gift with purchase' — per BRAND-GL-2026-001 Pricing Language, 'free' must specify conditions in the same line of copy. The current copy partially satisfies this ('free gift with purchase of $75 or more') but the word 'free' should be reviewed to confirm it meets the same-line conditions requirement in all creative executions (email, display, social). Warn issued pending creative execution review; no outright banned word violation found.

disclaimers.reason: The campaign copy states Star Rewards members get '25% off select Beauty items' — this is a flat percentage claim on a select assortment, which functions as a range claim because not all items will be discounted equally. Per LEGAL-DIS-2026-002 (Pricing Claims, Up To Claims) and BRAND-GL-2026-001 (Pricing Language), any 'up to X percent off' or selective discount claim must include the minimum discount available: e.g., 'Up to 25 percent off, starting at [Y] percent off.' The current copy omits the required 'starting at' minimum disclosure. This mirrors the pattern in COMP-EX-2026-001 Example 2 ('Up to 50 percent off Home Refresh' flagged for missing minimum). Additionally, the copy references a Star Rewards member benefit without a disclaimer clarifying enrollment or program terms, which may be required under LEGAL-DIS-2026-002. Required fix: add 'starting at [minimum]% off' to the discount claim and add Star Rewards program terms disclosure.

pricing_cross_check.reason: The check_pricing_conflicts tool returned catalog lookup failures for all three SKUs (MAC-001, EL-001, CLQ-001) — none were found in the active product catalog. This is itself a blocking issue: SKUs that cannot be resolved cannot be validated for MAP compliance or discount eligibility. Beyond the catalog failure, SKU prefix analysis against PRICE-RULES-2026-001 strongly indicates MAP exposure: EL-001 maps to Estée Lauder and CLQ-001 maps to Clinique, both of which are explicitly listed as MAP-enforced brands requiring written Merchandising approval before any discount is advertised. A 25% discount on these brands without documented Merchandising sign-off would violate PRICE-RULES-2026-001 and risk vendor chargebacks or account loss (see COMP-EX-2026-001 Example 9 for precedent). Required fixes: (1) resolve all three SKU IDs in the product catalog before resubmission; (2) obtain written Merchandising approval for any Estée Lauder and Clinique SKUs included in the 25% off offer; (3) confirm MAC-001 brand identity and MAP status with Merchandising.

step6b_brief.campaign_goal: Drive incremental revenue and brand engagement among VIP Loyalists during the Mother's Day gifting window through a curated prestige Beauty event with a 25% discount across three SKUs in four U.S. regions.
step6b_brief.target_audience: VIP Loyalists — high-value customers with active Star Rewards accounts and prior prestige Beauty purchase history, targeted across NY, CA, FL, and TX.
step6b_brief.expected_roi: Based on RETRO-Q4-2025, the Beauty Loyalists segment outperformed plan by 23%, with email open rates of 41% (vs. a 28% target) and conversion at 1.6x the segment average; no Mother's Day-specific spring beauty benchmark was available in retrieved retros, so Q4 Holiday figures represent the closest comparable.
risk_flags: PRICING CONFLICT — FAIL: check_pricing_conflicts returned status 'fail' for all three SKUs (MAC-001, EL-001, CLQ-001); none were found in the active product catalog. Discounting cannot be validated and MAP compliance for Estée Lauder (EL-001) and Clinique (CLQ-001), both MAP-enforced brands, cannot be confirmed until SKUs are resolved.
CATALOG INTEGRITY — FAIL: All three campaign SKUs are unresolvable in the catalog system. Campaign cannot activate until valid SKU IDs are confirmed with Merchandising.
MISSING CAMPAIGN MANAGER: The campaign_manager field is null. No owner is assigned for post-launch retro, revision routing, or activation accountability — required per FAQ-INT-2026-001.

MAP BRAND RISK: Estée Lauder and Clinique are on the MAP-enforced brand list under PRICE-RULES-2026-001. Even if SKUs are corrected, a 25% discount must be verified against MAP floors before approval.

COMPLIANCE CHECK NOT RUN: compliance_check is null in workflow state, meaning the standard pre-check gate was not completed prior to VP submission. Brief is based on direct MCP tool verification only.

SPEND TIER NOTE: Estimated spend of $200,000 is below the $500K VP+Legal dual-approval threshold (ref: TICKET-INC-2025-4471), so no Legal co-sign is required at this tier — but Legal pre-clearance on any comparative claims in final copy is recommended per Q4-2025 retro lessons.
step6b_brief.ai_recommendation: revise — The check_pricing_conflicts tool returned a hard 'fail' on all three SKUs (catalog not found), MAP compliance for two enforced brands cannot be confirmed at 25% off, and no campaign manager is assigned; the campaign must not proceed to activation until valid SKUs are submitted, MAP clearance is obtained, and an owner is designated.

report.executive_summary:
**Campaign Overview**

The Mother's Day Beauty Event (Campaign ID: MDC-2026-MD-001) is a Beauty category campaign targeting the General audience segment with a 25% discount offer. The campaign was submitted for workflow processing under status "submitted." At the time of this report, the campaign brief has been logged and entered the 10-step production workflow; however, step outputs for Steps 1–9 are not yet recorded in the current state, indicating the campaign is in early-stage processing and has not yet completed the full workflow cycle.

**Key Decisions and Workflow Status**

Because Steps 1–9 have not yet produced recorded outputs, key downstream decisions — including final audience segment refinement, SKU selection and lock, compliance review findings, copy development, locale variant generation, and approval recommendation — remain pending. The campaign brief establishes the foundational parameters: Beauty category, General segment, 25% discount depth, and a Mother's Day event framing. No SKUs have been locked, no copy has been drafted, and no compliance or approval determinations have been made at this stage. The audit log is currently empty, meaning no decisions, escalations, or rejections have been recorded against this campaign ID.

**Benchmarking Context**

Retro data from the Spring 2025 Beauty campaign (RETRO-SP-2025-BTY) provides relevant performance benchmarks for this event. That campaign delivered $42.1M in revenue against a $39.3M plan, a 32% email open rate versus a 26% segment average, a paid social ROAS of 4.2 against a 3.5 target, and an 18% in-store conversion uplift in the Beauty department. The Beauty Discovery sub-segment — customers who browsed but did not purchase in the prior 90 days — converted at 2.1x the segment baseline, driven primarily by a sampling offer. These benchmarks suggest that the current General segment targeting may underperform relative to a more precisely defined Beauty Discovery or lapsed-buyer segment, and that an incentive mechanic beyond a straight discount (e.g., a sampling offer) could meaningfully lift conversion.

**Risks and Concerns**

The most significant risk at this stage is that the campaign is proceeding with a General audience designation rather than a higher-performing targeted segment. Historical retro data consistently shows that segmented Beauty campaigns outperform General audience campaigns in both open rate and conversion. Additionally, the approval ticket from the Memorial Day 2025 Home campaign (TICKET-INC-2025-4471) documents that two preventable revision cycles cost approximately three production days — one due to insufficient Brand review rigor and one due to a comparative claim that was not pre-cleared with Legal at kickoff. These lessons are directly applicable here: Legal should be engaged early on any promotional claim methodology, and Brand review should apply a higher revision bar before advancing copy. Finally, with no step outputs yet recorded, there is a reporting completeness risk; this report should be refreshed once Steps 1–9 are finalized.

**Recommendations for Next Steps and Future Cycles**

For this campaign, the team should prioritize segment refinement in Step 1 — specifically evaluating a Beauty Discovery or lapsed-buyer cut against the General segment — and engage Legal at kickoff on the 25% discount claim and any comparative or "best value" language before copy is drafted. For the next campaign cycle, the retro process should be scheduled within four weeks of campaign close per internal FAQ guidance (FAQ-INT-2026-001), with Marketing Operations owning the retro template and action item tracking. Incorporating a sampling or value-add mechanic alongside the discount, as demonstrated in the Spring 2025 Beauty retro, should be evaluated as a conversion lever. This report will require a full refresh once all step outputs are available.
